title: "Create With Me" with Resident Artist Jessica Shiner
PNCR Outdoors All Day Event
description:
Join the City of Lancaster, Let’s Go 123, Lancaster Rec, the Friends of Reservoir Park, and the Pennsylvania Department of Conservation and Natural Resources (DCNR) for an Outdoors for All event on Saturday, July 25, from 11:00am to 3:00pm at Lancaster Reservoir Park, 832 E. Orange St., Lancaster. 
Launched in 2024, Outdoors for All Day celebrates the value of accessible, welcoming outdoor spaces across Pennsylvania. What began as a single celebration has grown into Outdoors for All Month each July. 
This year’s event will be a fun celebration featuring organizations from across the Lancaster region that help people connect with outdoor recreation, nature, and community. Visitors can enjoy interactive family friendly activities, environmental education, games, music, food, and more. 
Registration is optional but helps event organizers plan for language interpreters and additional logistics.

title: Valley Forge Park River Trail (Pawlings Rd)
description:
Walking Tails
Directions: From the intersection of Egypt Road and Park Ave./Pawlings Road, proceed on Pawlings Road heading towards the Schuylkill River. You will pass Mill Grove on your right, St. Gabriel Hall on your left and Pawling Farm on your left. You are getting close when you pass Sullivan Blvd. on your left and Gertrude St. on your right. You turn left on the next and last left (right before you go over the bridge over the Schuylkill River). Look for the River Trail Valley Forge Park sign visible from Pawlings Road. The gravel parking lot is straight ahead and also visible from Pawlings Road. If you go over the bridge over the Schuylkill River, you have gone too far and are now in Chester county.

CLICK DIRECTLY ON THE MAP IF YOU THINK YOU ARE LOST. IT WILL BRING YOU RIGHT TO US WHERE WE MEET.

This walk goes out about 1.5 miles along the Schuylkill River and then we come back the way we came, for a total of 3 miles. This is a dirt/gravel/mulch trail through the woods.

Start Time: Arrive a few minutes early. We will start hiking promptly at the scheduled time.

Duration of the walk – depends on the people and dogs in the group. We frequently end up walking in smaller packs based on the comfort level of the participants.

In the past this walk takes a little over an hour.

Please remember pooh bags and that your dog must be on a leash that is no more than 10 feet long. Sturdy shoes or hiking boots are recommended. Dress appropriately for weather conditions.

NOTICE: By attending this event you are agreeing that YOU ARE RESPONSIBLE FOR YOUR OWN SAFETY AT ALL TIMES. The hike leader and other members cannot be held responsible for any damages, accidents, or liabilities incurred while hiking with us.

Valley Forge Trail Map ([http://www.nps.gov/vafo/planyourvisit/maps.htm](http://www.nps.gov/vafo/planyourvisit/maps.htm))

title: Children's Chapel
location: Saint James Episcopal Church, 103 North Duke Street, Lancaster, PA, 17602, United States
description:
Children’s Chapel* meets weekly during the 10:30 AM Sunday Mass. Children and youth ages 3 and above begin the morning in the sanctuary where they can experience the processional and the opening congregational prayers. 
After the opening Collect, children are invited to the front of the sanctuary to make their way to the chapel and participate in songs, prayers, brief meditation and storytelling of the day’s Gospel and/or New and Old Testament readings. 
The Godly Play® teaching method includes using beautiful wooden figures, candles, and symbolic colors to aid our storytelling as we listen to God’s word for us. Children often respond to the story using simple art supplies including crayons, construction paper, origami paper and Model Magic air dry clay. 
Children return to the Sanctuary during the passing of the Peace. They are welcome to take part in Holy Communion.

title: Evening Compline
location: Saint James Episcopal Church, 103 North Duke Street, Lancaster, PA, 17602, United States
description:
Evening Compline
via Zoom
Click here to join Compline. (This link can be used for every evening Compline on Zoom.) 

The short service of Compline is based on the closing time of prayer in the Daily Office, or monastic cycle of prayer. It is observed in monasteries around 8 or 9 PM when darkness has fallen and bedtime is near. 

The thoughts that inspire the prayers during Compline are the need for divine forgiveness and protection against the powers of darkness. Prayers for peace and rest are offered as night falls. 

People of all faiths and beliefs are invited to this contemplative service. The service lasts about 20 minutes.

description:
The School District of Lancaster is inviting community members to become part of Valued Volunteers – Together We Read, a districtwide initiative that connects volunteers with students to help strengthen reading skills on Monday, July 27, at 1:00 pm – 3:00 pm at Burrowes Elementary School located at 101 Ranck Ave. Lancaster PA.  
The training serves as both the district’s required Valued Volunteers orientation and a kickoff for the Together We Read initiative. Participants will learn about the volunteer process while also receiving reading strategies, tips, and resources they can use when reading with students in our schools. 
No teaching experience is necessary. If you’re a first-time volunteer or returning to support SDoL students, the training will provide the tools and confidence needed to make every reading session meaningful. 
 
Volunteers play an important role in helping students build literacy skills and a love of reading. By sharing your time, you can make a lasting difference in a child’s educational journey. 
Join us for an upcoming Valued Volunteers – Together We Read training and discover how you can help students grow, one story at a time.

description:

Swoon Squad is a romance-centered book club with a twist. Instead of everyone reading the same assigned title, we choose a monthly trope and invite you to pick any book that fits the theme! Whether you're into sweet contemporary rom-coms, high-heat historical reads, or paranormal romance, there's a seat for you at our table! How it Works: Pick Your Own Adventure: We announce the month's trope, and you choose a book from your own TBR pile or the library shelves that features it. The short service of Compline is based on the closing time of prayer in the Daily Office, or monastic cycle of prayer. It is observed in monasteries around 8 or 9 PM when darkness has fallen and bedtime is near. 

The thoughts that inspire the prayers during Compline are the need for divine forgiveness and protection against the powers of darkness. Prayers for peace and rest are offered as night falls. 

People of all faiths and beliefs are invited to this contemplative service. The service lasts about 20 minutes.

title: Lancaster Breakfast and History Walking Tour
location: Unique Lancaster, 23 N Walnut Street, Lancaster, 17603, United States
description:
Searching for a walking history tour in Lancaster? You’re in for a flavorful experience—literally! 


Introducing the Lancaster History & Breakfast Walking Tour—a dynamic two-hour adventure that blends the rich heritage of one of America’s oldest inland cities with a delicious morning meal. Explore Lancaster’s vibrant streets with a professionally trained local guide and journey through time from the early 1700s through the transformative decades of the 20th century. 


Brought to you by Unique Lancaster Experiences, this guided walk kicks off with your choice of hot or iced coffee or tea to energize your morning. Along the way, you’ll hear engaging stories about Lancaster’s evolution as a bustling Market City and its transition from trolleys to automobiles after WWI. 


But this isn’t your standard history tour. You’ll dive into interactive discussions and uncover captivating insights about colonial life, architectural landmarks, and the impact of prohibition on the region. 


As you explore, you’ll stop at five handpicked local spots to enjoy a curated tasting menu featuring hearty breakfast sandwiches, fresh fruits, sweet pastries, and other morning favorites. 


Please note: This tour offers vegetarian-friendly options only. If you have other dietary needs, we recommend our International Food Tour for a better fit. 


Whether you’re passionate about history, love discovering new flavors, or just want a memorable way to see the city, the Lancaster History & Breakfast Tour is a great choice for solo explorers, couples, and groups alike.

title: Pennsylvania Wildlife Presented by Miller's Wildlife
description:
Summer Reading, Everyone

How well do you know your wild neighbors? Pennsylvania is famous for its extensive forests, but you don't have to go deep into the woods to learn about your wild neighbors! During our Pennsylvania Wildlife program, Patrick will introduce you to several Pennsylvania native birds and reptiles - some of which, you may find in your own backyard! From the skies of downtown Harrisburg to the farmlands of Lancaster County, each ecosystem has its own important wildlife to appreciate and protect. Join us as we discuss the ways that you can keep Pennsylvania's wilderness vast and diverse!Due to Pennsylvania Game Laws, participants attending the program are NOT permitted to touch the animals at any time. Program will be held at St. John's Evangelical Lutheran Church. Please enter on the 6th Street side at the RED Doors.Part of our 2026 Summer Reading program series. title: Lit Lovers Book Group
description:
Book Club, Adults

Lit Lovers is an eclectic reading group with a primary focus on fiction, while also exploring memoirs, short stories, biographies and autobiographies, mysteries, science fiction, and select works of nonfiction. The group is known for its lively, thoughtful discussions and makes a concerted effort to respect differing viewpoints. To keep conversations focused and meaningful, social chatter, gossip, and romance novels are generally kept outside the allotted discussion time.Lit Lovers gravitate toward modern fiction distinguished by strong writing, well-developed characters, and compelling narratives. Common themes include contemporary issues, family conflict, and the triumph of the human spirit, with a healthy appreciation for humor. Members read for both personal enrichment and enjoyment, and the group frequently selects works by international authors, books set abroad, or stories that explore multicultural perspectives.For a list of this year's book selections, click on the photo to the left or pick up a bookmark at the library!

location: Saint James Episcopal Church, 103 North Duke Street, Lancaster, PA, 17602, United States
description:
Evening Compline
via Zoom
Click here to join Compline. (This link can be used for every evening Compline on Zoom.) 

The short service of Compline is based on the closing time of prayer in the Daily Office, or monastic cycle of prayer. It is observed in monasteries around 8 or 9 PM when darkness has fallen and bedtime is near. 

The thoughts that inspire the prayers during Compline are the need for divine forgiveness and protection against the powers of darkness. Prayers for peace and rest are offered as night falls. 

People of all faiths and beliefs are invited to this contemplative service. The service lasts about 20 minutes.

via Zoom
Click here to join Compline. (This link can be used for every evening Compline on Zoom.) 

The short service of Compline is based on the closing time of prayer in the Daily Office, or monastic cycle of prayer. It is observed in monasteries around 8 or 9 PM when darkness has fallen and bedtime is near. 

The thoughts that inspire the prayers during Compline are the need for divine forgiveness and protection against the powers of darkness. Prayers for peace and rest are offered as night falls. 

People of all faiths and beliefs are invited to this contemplative service. The service lasts about 20 minutes.

title: Evening Compline
location: Saint James Episcopal Church, 103 North Duke Street, Lancaster, PA, 17602, United States
description:
Evening Compline
via Zoom
Click here to join Compline. (This link can be used for every evening Compline on Zoom.) 

The short service of Compline is based on the closing time of prayer in the Daily Office, or monastic cycle of prayer. It is observed in monasteries around 8 or 9 PM when darkness has fallen and bedtime is near. 

The thoughts that inspire the prayers during Compline are the need for divine forgiveness and protection against the powers of darkness. Prayers for peace and rest are offered as night falls. 

People of all faiths and beliefs are invited to this contemplative service. The service lasts about 20 minutes.

Spend an inspiring evening with Jeremy Camp, one of contemporary Christian music’s most influential and enduring artists. Known for his powerful blend of worship and rock, Camp has spent more than two decades creating music that connects deeply with audiences through messages of hope, perseverance, and faith. 
With chart-topping songs like “I Still Believe,” “Walk by Faith,” and “There Will Be a Day,” his live performances are both uplifting and deeply personal—bringing together heartfelt storytelling and dynamic musicianship.

description:
Living the Experience is a spiritual, interactive reenactment of the Underground Railroad. This Underground Railroad living history program is presented interactively in first person in an effort to bring alive the people, places, and events of Lancaster. The program actively engages its audiences in the storytelling of Lancaster’s involvement in the Underground Railroad and also its involvement as a free community of Africans.  



Those who attend are provided an honest portrayal of the experiential realities of those involved in the Underground Railroad through the stories that are told, the spirituals that are sung, and in the emotional connections that are felt. Attendees will learn and gain a clearer perspective on the events and the people involved with this “station” on the underground railroad. Following the reenactment, a Southern style meal is served, and local vendors are on site. Step into history like never before. Come Live the Experience!

title: Ben & Rose with Conrad Fisher
location: American Music Theatre, 2425 Lincoln Hwy East, Lancaster, PA, 17605, United States
description:
Tickets: $29 $34 $39 
Ben & Rose are more than just a duo — they’re a harmony born of Lancaster County’s Plain Community, where tradition, faith, and family shape every note. Their music carries the quiet strength of country roads and the timeless beauty of rural life, weaving humility and heart into every song. Blending country, folk, and gospel, Ben & Rose create music that is both tender and timeless. Their young voices lock together like old friends, evoking front-porch evenings, Sunday hymns, and the kind of stories that linger long after the last note. Each performance is a reminder that simple living can yield the richest music — songs filled with love, hope, and the rhythms of everyday grace. 
Their journey began as teenagers singing side by side, finding harmonies to Lady Antebellum tracks at local youth gatherings. What started at karaoke nights grew into something far deeper: a loving marriage and a shared passion for storytelling through song. Today, their harmonies carry the same spark of those early days, polished by years of life, love, and laughter together. 
Ben & Rose often collaborate with fellow Plain Community songwriter Conrad Fisher, whose work has been recorded by legends like the Oak Ridge Boys, Rhonda Vincent, and The Malpass Brothers. Together, they craft music that feels both rooted and refreshing — a modern echo of simpler times, celebrating the beauty found in everyday life.

title: Patriarchy, Matriarchy & Democracy: A Two-Part Online Discussion
description:
Lancaster Freethought Society
**A Two-Part Online Discussion: Can Democracy Survive a Patriarchy?**
This is an LFS online discussion series, held on Google Meet.

Across two sessions, we’ll explore how patriarchy and matriarchy organize power, care, law, family, sex, money, violence, and democracy.
We’ll use consciousness-raising style discussion rules: speak personally, listen carefully, don’t interrupt, and don’t debate someone while they are speaking.

For each question, we’ll do a speaking round first. After everyone who wants to speak has spoken, Susan will offer brief evidence, examples, or definitions to deepen the discussion.

**Part 1**

* What is patriarchy?
* What is matriarchy?
* How do these systems operate?

**Part 2**

* What are the benefits of each?
* What are the dangers or pitfalls of each?
* Can democracy survive a patriarchy — or does real democracy require a different social order?

This is not a lecture. It is a structured conversation.

**Google Meet link:** The Google Meet link will be sent on the day and only to members who RSVP “Yes.” Please RSVP if you plan to attend.

This event welcomes open inquiry and diverse viewpoints within a foundation of equality, human dignity, and democracy. Racist, sexist, fascist, anti-LGBTQ, or other ideologies that deny anyone’s equal rights are not welcome or open for debate. Participants will not be required to defend or debate their humanity or equality. The organizer may interrupt or remove anyone whose words or conduct violate these boundaries.

title: LUNA Dance Company: First Friday Preview Performance
location: Ware Center for the Arts, 42 N. Prince St., Lancaster, PA, 17603, United States
description:
Experience an exciting preview of LUNA Dance Company’s upcoming Season 6 performance in this special First Friday event. As Lancaster’s professional contemporary dance company, LUNA is committed to expanding access to exceptional dance experiences by bringing high-level performances, nationally recognized artists, and professional training opportunities to our local community.  



The evening will feature two original contemporary works showcasing the athleticism, artistry, and storytelling that define LUNA’s work. Audiences will also experience a unique live choreographic collaboration as Artistic Director Emmanuel Williams creates a brand-new piece in real time using prompts from the audience, offering a rare opportunity to witness the creative process unfold live on stage. Following the performance, stay for an interactive Q&A with Artistic Director Emmanuel Williams and LUNA’s dancers. Learn more about the creative process, ask questions about the works you’ve seen, and gain a behind-the-scenes perspective on what it takes to create and perform contemporary dance. Whether you’re a longtime dance enthusiast or experiencing contemporary dance for the first time, this interactive evening offers a unique opportunity to engage with the artists while previewing LUNA’s full Season 6 performance on September 26. Join us for an evening of creativity, collaboration, and conversation as LUNA continues cultivating professional contemporary dance in Lancaster.

title: Craig Morgan
location: American Music Theatre, 2425 Lincoln Hwy East, Lancaster, PA, 17605, United States
description:
Tickets: $49 $59 $69 $79 
Known for his signature blend of heartfelt ballads and high-energy anthems, Morgan has built a career rooted in real-life experiences, patriotism, and a deep connection to his fans. His chart-topping hits include “Redneck Yacht Club,” “That’s What I Love About Sunday,” “International Harvester,” and “Almost Home,” songs that capture the spirit of everyday life with honesty and heart. 
Before his rise in country music, Morgan proudly served in the U.S. Army, a background that continues to shape both his music and his character. His dedication to service and community has earned him widespread respect, including recognition from organizations supporting military members and veterans. 
On stage, Craig Morgan delivers a powerful live show filled with energy, humor, and genuine connection. Whether he’s sharing stories behind his songs or leading the crowd in a singalong, his performances feel as personal as they are entertaining. 
For certain concerts, audience members may prefer to stand or dance, especially when encouraged by the artist to do so. Guest expectations differ, so we simply ask all attendees to extend mutual respect toward one another and maintain awareness of those around them. Our staff will only intervene in matters of safety or when behavior is deemed unruly, combative, or disruptive to the overall performance.

title: Creative Release Open Studio Saturday
description:
The Creative House of Lancaster
#### ***A Place to Make Art Together***

**When:** Every Other Saturday from 10am - 12pm
**Where:** [The Candy Factory](https://share.google/nqC7VtCS6IcDeBRyg)
**Cost:** Free & Open to the Public
**Ages:** All Ages

**Upcoming Dates**
July 11, July 25, Aug 8, Aug 22, Sept 5, Sept 19, Oct 3, Oct 17, Oct 31, Nov 14, Nov 28, Dec 9, Dec 23

*Do you have creative aspirations but never seem to make the time? Do you want the companionship of others to overcome your creative blocks and “just do it”?*

Creative Release provides spaces and resources that make artmaking accessible. Whether you’re an experienced artist or just looking to explore your creative side, Creative Release is a safe place to explore your ideas with others. Bring your ongoing projects or use the art materials available.

Don't have a project at the moment? That's just fine. I’ll have materials to share.
**What to Expect:**

* A welcoming, inclusive environment
* A variety of art materials to experiment with
* Demonstrations on how to use different art materials
* The opportunity to work on your personal projects
* The chance to meet and collaborate with fellow creatives
* A moment to relax, create, and escape the usual routine

**Who Should Join?**
Anyone and everyone! Bring an idea for a card, a knitting pattern you’ve been wanting to try, a shirt that needs mending, or a full-on canvas and paints. Most of all, bring your lovely self! We believe in the power of community and creativity.

[Event Link](https://www.jodavis.art/community-events-1/creative-release)

location: American Music Theatre, 2425 Lincoln Hwy East, Lancaster, PA, 17605, United States
description:
Tickets: $39 $59 $69 $79 
The Great American Tour is a celebration of the timeless music that defined a generation—and continues to resonate today. Baby Boomers have never lost their passion for the “oldies but goodies” of the 1960s and 70s, and this unforgettable show delivers the songs that shaped youth, freedom, and the unifying power of rock ’n roll. Featuring iconic artists inducted into the Vocal Group Hall of Fame, this tour brings together legendary performers whose hits remain woven into modern movies, television, and commercials, captivating audiences across generations. 
Headlining the tour are Jay and the Americans, one of the era’s few groups still featuring two original members. With an incredible legacy that includes 19 charted hits and 9 Top 40 records, the group continues to thrive with over 900,000 monthly Spotify listeners. Their smash hit “Come a Little Bit Closer”—famously featured in Guardians of the Galaxy—has amassed more than 190 million streams, while classics like “This Magic Moment,” “Cara Mia,” “Walkin’ in the Rain,” and “Only in America” remain beloved fan favorites. 
Joining them are The Classics IV, renowned for their instantly recognizable sound and million-selling, Gold Disc–winning hits “Spooky,” “Traces,” and “Stormy.” Also appearing are Vocal Group Hall of Fame inductees Jay Siegel’s Tokens, led by original frontman Jay Siegel, still thrilling audiences with soaring falsettos on classics such as “Tonight I Fell In Love,” “I Hear Trumpets Blow,” and the immortal “The Lion Sleeps Tonight,” a song continually rediscovered through The Lion King on Broadway and film. 
Perfect for audiences eager to relive cherished memories—or introduce younger generations to the music that started it all—The Great American Tour delivers enduring hits with heart, harmony, and history. 
For certain concerts, audience members may prefer to stand or dance, especially when encouraged by the artist to do so. Guest expectations differ, so we simply ask all attendees to extend mutual respect toward one another and maintain awareness of those around them. Our staff will only intervene in matters of safety or when behavior is deemed unruly, combative, or disruptive to the overall performance.

title: Patriarchy, Matriarchy & Democracy: A Two-Part Online Discussion
description:
Lancaster Freethought Society
This is an LFS online discussion series, held on Google Meet.
Across two sessions, we’ll explore how patriarchy and matriarchy organize power, care, law, family, sex, money, violence, and democracy.
We’ll use consciousness-raising style discussion rules: speak personally, listen carefully, don’t interrupt, and don’t debate someone while they are speaking.
For each question, we’ll do a speaking round first. After everyone who wants to speak has spoken, Susan will offer brief evidence, examples, or definitions to deepen the discussion.

**Part 2 August 13**

* What are the benefits of each?
* What are the dangers or pitfalls of each?
* Can democracy exist inside a patriarchy?

This is not a lecture. It is a structured conversation about power, equality, family, sex, law, care, violence, democracy, and what kind of world we want to build.

This event welcomes open inquiry and diverse viewpoints within a foundation of equality, human dignity, and democracy. Racist, sexist, fascist, anti-LGBTQ, or other ideologies that deny anyone’s equal rights are not welcome or open for debate. Participants will not be required to defend or debate their humanity or equality. The organizer may interrupt or remove anyone whose words or conduct violate these boundaries.

title: A Bronx Tale: One Man Show Starring Chazz Palminteri
location: American Music Theatre, 2425 Lincoln Hwy East, Lancaster, PA, 17605, United States
description:
Tickets: $39 $49 $59 $79 
Bronx-born and raised Chazz Palminteri wrote A Bronx Tale in 1988. The powerful one-man stage play depicted his bruising childhood which included witnessing a gangland killing when he was nine years old. Palminteri played 18 characters and brought them all to life in his autobiographical play. His friends, enemies and family came alive on stage. Hollywood Studios went crazy after seeing it and offered him millions of dollars to turn it into a major movie. There was one catch… They wanted to put a star in the role of Sonny and someone else to write the screenplay. With $200 dollars in the bank…Palminteri said No… he would hold out and wait. He wanted to play Sonny and write the screenplay. Then one night, Palminteri walked into his dressing room and siting there was Robert De Niro who just saw the show… He said it was the greatest one-man show he’s ever seen. Robert DeNiro gave Palminteri the chance he was waiting for… And as they say in Hollywood the rest is history.  Palminteri wrote the screenplay for the film A Bronx Tale and then most recently wrote the book for the Broadway Musical. It was the first time in history that the same actor wrote the one-man play, the movie, and the Broadway Musical and starred in each one. The show you will see now is the exact show Chazz Palminteri did 34 years ago with just a chair that made him a star.

title: The Doo Wop Project: Echoes of the Street
location: American Music Theatre, 2425 Lincoln Hwy East, Lancaster, PA, 17605, United States
description:
Tickets: $29 $39 $49 
The dynamic Broadway stars of The Doo Wop Project are on a mission to put Doo Wop on everyone’s playlist! With their smokin’ hot band, they capture and deliver the classic sounds of the guys who, back in the day, harmonized with each other on stoops, in the subway, and on street corners, and they have also created a unique, exciting, fun way to “Doowop-ify” today’s biggest hits – reimagining them as though they had been written during the Doo Wop era! Once you experience The Doo Wop Project live on stage, you’ll see why everyone around the country calls them AMERICA’S PREMIERE DOO WOP GROUP. 
Their brand new 90 minute show — “Echoes of the Street” — keeps the classic sounds of Doo Wop alive for audiences of all ages. You’ll hear Doo Wop classics like the Del Vikings’ “Whispering Bells”, The Tymes’ “So Much in Love”, The Marcels’ “Blue Moon”, The Four Seasons’ “Sherry” and Motown’s “My Girl”. And you’ll fall in love with The Doo Wop Project’s Doowop-ified versions of contemporary songs by artists like Taylor Swift, Pharell Williams and Daft Punk. 
This show celebrates a music genre that has never lost its cool….while making it cool for generations to come. #SAVEDOOWOP

This presentation reveals the "forest pharmacy" of medicinal plants, the expert craftsmanship behind essential tools, and the architectural secrets of early housing. Join us to reconnect with the deep, hidden history of the land we call home.

title: Blue Öyster Cult
location: American Music Theatre, 2425 Lincoln Hwy East, Lancaster, PA, 17605, United States
description:
Tickets: $59 $69 $79 $89 
For more than five decades, Blue Öyster Cult has thrilled audiences around the world with its signature blend of intelligent hard rock and heavy metal. Widely regarded as one of the genre’s most influential bands, BÖC has earned both critical acclaim and commercial success—an achievement few of their peers can claim. Their innovative sound and thought-provoking lyrics have inspired generations of artists, including bands like Metallica. 
From their self-titled debut in 1972 to today, Blue Öyster Cult has built a legendary catalog of music that balances power, melody, and mystique. Fans can expect to hear iconic hits like “(Don’t Fear) The Reaper,” “Godzilla,” and “Burnin’ for You,” along with a deep lineup of fan favorites including “Cities on Flame with Rock and Roll,” “Astronomy,” and “Veteran of the Psychic Wars.” 
Still touring relentlessly, the band continues to deliver electrifying live performances that showcase their enduring appeal and musicianship. With recent releases including The Symbol Remains and 2024’s Ghost Stories, Blue Öyster Cult proves their classic sound remains as vibrant and relevant as ever.

title: Creative Release Open Studio Saturday
description:
The Creative House of Lancaster
#### ***A Place to Make Art Together***

**When:** Every Other Saturday from 10am - 12pm
**Where:** [The Candy Factory](https://share.google/nqC7VtCS6IcDeBRyg)
**Cost:** Free & Open to the Public
**Ages:** All Ages

**Upcoming Dates**
July 11, July 25, Aug 8, Aug 22, Sept 5, Sept 19, Oct 3, Oct 17, Oct 31, Nov 14, Nov 28, Dec 9, Dec 23

*Do you have creative aspirations but never seem to make the time? Do you want the companionship of others to overcome your creative blocks and “just do it”?*

Creative Release provides spaces and resources that make artmaking accessible. Whether you’re an experienced artist or just looking to explore your creative side, Creative Release is a safe place to explore your ideas with others. Bring your ongoing projects or use the art materials available.

Don't have a project at the moment? That's just fine. I’ll have materials to share.
**What to Expect:**

* A welcoming, inclusive environment
* A variety of art materials to experiment with
* Demonstrations on how to use different art materials
* The opportunity to work on your personal projects
* The chance to meet and collaborate with fellow creatives
* A moment to relax, create, and escape the usual routine

**Who Should Join?**
Anyone and everyone! Bring an idea for a card, a knitting pattern you’ve been wanting to try, a shirt that needs mending, or a full-on canvas and paints. Most of all, bring your lovely self! We believe in the power of community and creativity.

[Event Link](https://www.jodavis.art/community-events-1/creative-release)

She is backed by a seven-piece band consisting of top-notch, professional industry musicians who have had amazing careers in their own right. The band members are all multi-instrumentalists and at times use 3 keyboards to recreate the incredibly complex arrangements created by Richard Carpenter. The attention to detail paired with saxophone, trumpet, flute and many more instruments complete every song to perfection!

No doubt, you will be singing along as they perform hits like; “Close To You”, “We’ve Only Just Begun”, “Rainy Days And Mondays”, “Please Mr. Postman” and “Yesterday Once More”, to name a few. title: Teen Book Talk:  What the River Knows
description:
Book Club, Teens

For Teens ages 13-18 years of age only.Calling all teen readers! Join us for Teen Book Talk, a fun and engaging monthly book discussion group led by members of our Teen Advisory Board! Book selections are chosen by teens during advisory meetings. Interested in joining the Teen Advisory Board? Sign up through the library calendar. Each month, we’ll dive into a new title—ranging from trending young adult fiction to graphic novels, fantasy epics, thought-provoking contemporary stories, and more.This month we'll be reading "What the River Knows" by Isabel Ibanez. Set in 1884, nineteen-year-old Inez travels to Egypt after the sudden death of her parents to uncover the truth about their deaths, and as she attempts to unravel the mysteries her parents sought, she becomes a pawn in a larger game that threatens to kill her.  You’ll get the chance to share your thoughts, hear different perspectives, and connect with fellow book lovers in a relaxed and welcoming space. Snacks will be provided, and occasionally we’ll have themed activities or giveaways tied to the book!Note: To help everyone stay present and get the most out of the experience, we ask that all phones stay in pockets or bags during the program. title: Lit Lovers Book Group
description:
Book Club, Adults

Lit Lovers is an eclectic reading group with a primary focus on fiction, while also exploring memoirs, short stories, biographies and autobiographies, mysteries, science fiction, and select works of nonfiction. The group is known for its lively, thoughtful discussions and makes a concerted effort to respect differing viewpoints. To keep conversations focused and meaningful, social chatter, gossip, and romance novels are generally kept outside the allotted discussion time.Lit Lovers gravitate toward modern fiction distinguished by strong writing, well-developed characters, and compelling narratives. Common themes include contemporary issues, family conflict, and the triumph of the human spirit, with a healthy appreciation for humor. Members read for both personal enrichment and enjoyment, and the group frequently selects works by international authors, books set abroad, or stories that explore multicultural perspectives.For a list of this year's book selections, click on the photo to the left or pick up a bookmark at the library!

title: Swoon Squad: A Romance TBR Book Club
description:
Book Club, Adults, Seniors

Swoon Squad is a romance-centered book club with a twist. Instead of everyone reading the same assigned title, we choose a monthly trope and invite you to pick any book that fits the theme! Whether you're into sweet contemporary rom-coms, high-heat historical reads, or paranormal romance, there's a seat for you at our table! How it Works: Pick Your Own Adventure: We announce the month's trope, and you choose a book from your own TBR pile or the library shelves that features it. Low Pressure, High Fun: No more scrambling to finish a specific book you might not even like. Read at your own pace and bring your honest thoughts! The Discussion: We gather to swap recommendations, vent about our favorite (and least favorite) clichés, and discover new authors through each other's picks.Come ready to share your pick, discuss the tropes, and meet fellow romance fans in a comfortable library setting ❤️June 29 - ⚔️Enemies to Lovers ⚔️July 27 - 🥰😠Grumpy/Sunshine😠🥰August 31 - 🏆Sports Romance🏆September 28 - 📖Academic Romance📖October 26 - 🧛Paranormal Romance🧛November 30 - 🛏️Forced Proximity🛏️December 28 - 🎁Holiday Romance🎁

Together we can help each other grow and expand our consciousness for these high vibrational times.

Donations Greatly Appreciated!

This Event is lovingly hosted By Anna Bojczuk. Anna is a Registered nurse with over 40 years of experience as well as a gifted Energy worker. Anna is also long-time volunteer and inspiration in the Being One Center Community.

Lancaster Freethought Society is a community for Freethinkers, Atheists, Agnostics, Humanists, Non-believers, Skeptics, and those who are simply curious. There is no fee to attend our meetings which range from topical subjects of interest to freethinkers such as Church/State Separation, as well as subjects such as science, philosophy, ethics, counter-apologetics, and psychology. description:
The Creative House of Lancaster
#### ***A Place to Make Art Together***

**When:** Every Other Saturday from 10am - 12pm
**Where:** [The Candy Factory](https://share.google/nqC7VtCS6IcDeBRyg)
**Cost:** Free & Open to the Public
**Ages:** All Ages

**Upcoming Dates**
July 11, July 25, Aug 8, Aug 22, Sept 5, Sept 19, Oct 3, Oct 17, Oct 31, Nov 14, Nov 28, Dec 9, Dec 23

*Do you have creative aspirations but never seem to make the time? Do you want the companionship of others to overcome your creative blocks and “just do it”?*

Creative Release provides spaces and resources that make artmaking accessible. Whether you’re an experienced artist or just looking to explore your creative side, Creative Release is a safe place to explore your ideas with others. Bring your ongoing projects or use the art materials available.

Don't have a project at the moment? That's just fine. I’ll have materials to share.
**What to Expect:**

* A welcoming, inclusive environment
* A variety of art materials to experiment with
* Demonstrations on how to use different art materials
* The opportunity to work on your personal projects
* The chance to meet and collaborate with fellow creatives
* A moment to relax, create, and escape the usual routine

**Who Should Join?**
Anyone and everyone! Bring an idea for a card, a knitting pattern you’ve been wanting to try, a shirt that needs mending, or a full-on canvas and paints. Most of all, bring your lovely self! We believe in the power of community and creativity.

[Event Link](https://www.jodavis.art/community-events-1/creative-release)

title: The Secret World of Pennsylvania’s Bats
location: Manheim Township, MTP Morgan Center B
description:

Think you know the night? Think again. Behind the myths and "spooky" tropes lies one of the most efficient biological machines on the planet. Pennsylvania’s bats are tactical hunters, essential ecosystem anchors, and currently, they are fighting an uphill battle for survival.Join the Lancaster County Department of Parks & Recreation for an unfiltered look at the state of our skies. We’re moving past the basics to explore the high-stakes world of our six hibernating species and the seasonal migrators that cross our borders. We’ll discuss the grim reality of a 99% population collapse and the cascading effect that has on our local environment—specifically when it comes to controlling the world’s most prolific killer: the mosquito.From the bizarre evolutionary traits of bats across the globe to the specific conservation strategies needed right here in Lancaster County, this program is designed for those who want the real story. Come find out why these masters of the dark are the most important neighbors you’ve never met, and how you can play a role in their recovery 🦇

title: W. Miller Barbour & His Prospect for Freedom
description:
Community, Presentation, Adults, Seniors

Join public historian Eric Schubert for a talk about a pioneering Pennsylvania human rights leader whose activism helped define mid-20th-century civil rights goals.Long before the modern Civil Rights Movement, W. Miller Barbour (1908–1957) dedicated his life to advancing racial equality and human rights. A Middletown native and Elizabethtown College graduate, Barbour rose from local roots to become a pioneering civil rights leader, serving with the Urban League in Denver and Los Angeles. Through advocacy, community organizing, and interracial dialogue, he expanded opportunities for African Americans decades before the landmark victories of the 1960s. This presentation explores Barbour’s remarkable journey from central Pennsylvania to the forefront of early civil rights activism and examines the enduring legacy of a forgotten champion for equality.Eric Schubert is a public historian, genealogist, and forensic genetic genealogist as seen on Good Morning America and more. He serves on the Executive Committee of the Historic Preservation Trust of Lancaster County and is a White House Historical Association Next-Gen Leader. Schubert earned his M.A. in History at Millersville University. He is part of the research team which contributed to the award-winning documentary The Prospect for Freedom: W. Miller Barbour's Human Rights Journey and organized the W. Miller Barbour Lecture Series alongside Abigail Sholes, which seeks to reintroduce Barbour’s legacy to communities across Pennsylvania.

title: Monthly Club Meeting - “Sparrows Simplified: Making Sense of LBJ’s”
location: North Museum of Nature and Science, 400 College Ave, Lancaster, PA, 17603, United States
description:
Club Meeting – North Museum of Nature and Science, 400 College Ave, Lancaster, PA 17603 
Presented by Michael Moore, retired Biology professor and past president of the Delaware Ornithological Society  
Many birders struggle with identifying sparrows, referring to them as LBJ’s (little brown jobs) or sparrow sp. This talk will help you tackle this difficult group. It will discuss and then attempt to blend the two main approaches to identification, the Peterson System and the Cape May School, to lead you to sparrow identification confidence. Each of the 16 species of regularly occurring sparrows in this area will be compared and contrasted with some discussion of finding and identifying rarities. 
Mike is a retired Biology Professor and a past president of the Delaware Ornithological Society. He started birding in middle school in Massachusetts and has had a life longpassion for birds. He completed his PhD at the University of Washington on the field endocrinology of White-crowned Sparrows. After doing a postdoc at the University of Texas in Austin, he served on the Biology Faculty at Arizona State University for 27 years.  He moved to the University of Delaware in in 2009 where he retired after 11 years. He has been funded throughout his career by the National Science Foundation and the Nation Institutes of Health and has published nearly 100 papers in scientific journals. He also has a passion for dragonflies and serves as a Vice President for the Dragonfly Society of the Americas.

Now, Costello returns to the stage with The Imposters and special guest Charlie Sexton for Radio Soul!: The Early Songs of Elvis Costello. 
This unforgettable live performance celebrates the groundbreaking early years of Costello’s career, featuring songs drawn from his first eleven albums — from My Aim Is True through Blood & Chocolate — including fan favorites, deep cuts, and the sharp lyrical storytelling that helped define an era. 
Backed by the powerhouse musicianship of The Imposters and the electrifying guitar work of Charlie Sexton, the evening promises a high-energy journey through some of Costello’s most iconic songs, blending raw rock & roll spirit with soulful melodies and biting wit.

description:
Tickets: $34 $44 $54 $64 
Get The Led Out (GTLO) brings the thunderous power, mystique, and musical depth of Led Zeppelin to the stage in a high-energy live concert experience. This Philadelphia-based group of six seasoned musicians delivers Zeppelin’s legendary catalog with stunning precision—recreating the layered studio sound in ways even Zeppelin never performed live. If the record features three guitars, GTLO brings three guitars to the stage. The result is a massive, immersive wall of sound that stays true to the original recordings while feeling fresh and electrifying in concert. 
Dubbed “The American Led Zeppelin,” GTLO dives deep into the band’s iconic early years while also spotlighting fan-favorite deep cuts rarely heard live. The show also features a special acoustic set, highlighting the more intimate side of Zeppelin with songs like “Tangerine” and “Hey Hey What Can I Do.” 
With a strong national touring history and performances at major theaters and performing arts centers across the country, GTLO is known for delivering Zeppelin’s music with both power and nuance. No costumes, no gimmicks—just an honest, heart-pounding celebration of one of rock’s greatest catalogs. For longtime fans and new listeners alike, a GTLO show captures the light, shade, passion, and fury of “The Mighty Zep” in a truly unforgettable live experience. 
For certain concerts, audience members may prefer to stand or dance, especially when encouraged by the artist to do so. Guest expectations differ, so we simply ask all attendees to extend mutual respect toward one another and maintain awareness of those around them. Our staff will only intervene in matters of safety or when behavior is deemed unruly, combative, or disruptive to the overall performance.

Celtic Thunder returns with an electrifying celebration of Irish music, storytelling, and powerful vocal harmony. Known around the world for their dynamic stage productions and charismatic performers, Celtic Thunder blends traditional Irish songs with contemporary favorites, delivering a concert experience that is both uplifting and unforgettable. 
Backed by a talented band and enhanced with dramatic lighting and theatrical staging, the group’s acclaimed vocalists bring passion and personality to every performance.  Register to attend: https://eastlampetertownship.org/departments/parks/#birdwalk

 In case of bad weather, cancellations will be announced the day before and registered participants will be notified.

title: ZZ Top: The Big One
location: American Music Theatre, 2425 Lincoln Hwy East, Lancaster, PA, 17605, United States
description:
Tickets: $99 $119 $139 $159
 
ZZ Top Silver Premium Ticket Package  $309 
Package includes 

(1) Ticket located in the first 15 rows of the venue
Limited edition ZZ Top merchandise – exclusive to VIP packages

Rock legends ZZ Top have been delivering their signature blend of blues, boogie, and hard rock for over half a century. Formed in Houston in 1969 by Billy Gibbons, Dusty Hill, and Frank Beard, the band rose to national prominence with Tres Hombres and the enduring hit “La Grange,” before reaching global superstardom with 1983’s Eliminator and iconic tracks like “Sharp Dressed Man” and “Legs.” 
Famed for their unmistakable look—long beards, hot rods, and spinning guitars—ZZ Top became one of MTV’s defining acts while staying true to their deep blues roots. Their influences span legends like Muddy Waters, B.B. King, and Jimi Hendrix, shaping a sound that is both timeless and instantly recognizable. 
With millions of records sold, decades of worldwide touring, and an induction into the Rock & Roll Hall of Fame by Keith Richards, ZZ Top remains one of the most enduring forces in rock. Following the passing of Dusty Hill, longtime guitar tech Elwood Francis stepped in on bass, helping carry the band’s legacy forward. 
Still going strong, ZZ Top continues to bring their trademark groove, grit, and swagger to audiences everywhere—driven by their enduring mantra: “Tone, Taste, and Tenacity.” 
For certain concerts, audience members may prefer to stand or dance, especially when encouraged by the artist to do so. Guest expectations differ, so we simply ask all attendees to extend mutual respect toward one another and maintain awareness of those around them. Our staff will only intervene in matters of safety or when behavior is deemed unruly, combative, or disruptive to the overall performance.

BEATLES, ZEPPELIN, DOORS by Magical Mystery Doors is a tribute act that blends and layers the music of three legendary bands to create something new and unique for music fans everywhere.

The melody from The Doors’ “Hello, I Love You” laying atop Led Zeppelin’s “Misty Mountain Hop.” The pounding beat of Zep’s “When The Levee Breaks” coupled with the serene strumming of The Beatles’ “Dear Prudence.” The thematic sequence of The Rain Song – Riders On The Storm – Here Comes The Sun. These rare arrangements take crowds on an unexpected and exhilarating journey “Over The Hills And Far Away.” 
MMD also enhances the audience experience with a captivating visual presentation. Modern video screens and a stunning array of lighting allow this act to create an environment where the music comes to life. Fans young and old can “Break On Through” their daily distractions in this immersive and mesmerizing show.

title: Creative Release Open Studio Saturday
description:
The Creative House of Lancaster
#### ***A Place to Make Art Together***

**When:** Every Other Saturday from 10am - 12pm
**Where:** [The Candy Factory](https://share.google/nqC7VtCS6IcDeBRyg)
**Cost:** Free & Open to the Public
**Ages:** All Ages

**Upcoming Dates**
July 11, July 25, Aug 8, Aug 22, Sept 5, Sept 19, Oct 3, Oct 17, Oct 31, Nov 14, Nov 28, Dec 9, Dec 23

*Do you have creative aspirations but never seem to make the time? Do you want the companionship of others to overcome your creative blocks and “just do it”?*

Creative Release provides spaces and resources that make artmaking accessible. Whether you’re an experienced artist or just looking to explore your creative side, Creative Release is a safe place to explore your ideas with others. Bring your ongoing projects or use the art materials available.

Don't have a project at the moment? That's just fine. I’ll have materials to share.
**What to Expect:**

* A welcoming, inclusive environment
* A variety of art materials to experiment with
* Demonstrations on how to use different art materials
* The opportunity to work on your personal projects
* The chance to meet and collaborate with fellow creatives
* A moment to relax, create, and escape the usual routine

**Who Should Join?**
Anyone and everyone! Bring an idea for a card, a knitting pattern you’ve been wanting to try, a shirt that needs mending, or a full-on canvas and paints. Most of all, bring your lovely self! We believe in the power of community and creativity.

[Event Link](https://www.jodavis.art/community-events-1/creative-release)

Experience the music, story, and legacy of one of America’s most beloved singer-songwriters with The Billy Joel Legacy: Celebrating the Piano Man. From the producers of The Simon and Garfunkel Story and The Life and Music of George Michael, this captivating concert event takes audiences on a journey through Billy Joel’s remarkable career—from his Long Island beginnings to international superstardom. Featuring faithful recreations of his greatest hits, stunning multimedia visuals, and engaging storytelling, The Billy Joel Legacy brings classics like “Piano Man,” “Uptown Girl,” “We Didn’t Start the Fire,” “New York State of Mind,” and more to life on stage. More than a tribute concert, this is a heartfelt celebration of Billy Joel’s extraordinary contribution to music and culture.

title: Rhonda Vincent with The Malpass Brothers
location: American Music Theatre, 2425 Lincoln Hwy East, Lancaster, PA, 17605, United States
description:
Tickets: $29 $39 $49 $69 
Rhonda Vincent is a powerhouse performer whose fiery talent and unmistakable voice have made her one of the most celebrated artists in bluegrass music. Hailing from Greentop, Missouri, Rhonda’s musical roots run five generations deep. She began performing professionally at just five years old with her family’s band, The Sally Mountain Show, gaining early experience on stage, radio, and television. By her teens, she had mastered multiple instruments and developed the work ethic and passion that would define her career. 
Her journey took a pivotal turn when a chance performance led to an invitation from the Grand Ole Opry—an early sign of the remarkable path ahead. Rhonda went on to build an award-winning career, earning the title “New Queen of Bluegrass” and becoming known for her signature blend of traditional roots and contemporary energy. Her breakthrough album Back Home Again cemented her status as a leading voice in the genre. 
A Grammy Award winner and one of the most decorated artists in bluegrass history, Rhonda Vincent has earned numerous honors, including multiple International Bluegrass Music Association Female Vocalist of the Year awards and Entertainer of the Year. In 2021, she achieved a lifelong dream with her official induction into the Grand Ole Opry. 
With a voice that transcends genres and collaborations that include artists like Dolly Parton, Rhonda Vincent continues to captivate audiences with high-energy performances, world-class musicianship, and a deep-rooted love of the music that started it all. 
As young boys, The Malpass Brothers – Christopher and Taylor – soaked up the music of their granddad’s phonograph records.  Christopher earned his first talent show trophy at age 7, and Taylor was playing mandolin by the time he was 10.  Today, they promote the work and music of classic country artists they treasure while creating new music and making their own mark in the lineage of a rich American cultural heritage.  With sincerity, honesty, and an utter ease on stage that belies their years, their smooth vocal blend and skillful musicianship layer infectiously into the deep respect they pay to legends who have paved the way.  Add the funny, off-the-cuff quips between the two 20-something siblings, and the engaging concert becomes a magnetic time-traveling journey to when a calmer rhythm reigned supreme. 
For certain concerts, audience members may prefer to stand or dance, especially when encouraged by the artist to do so. Guest expectations differ, so we simply ask all attendees to extend mutual respect toward one another and maintain awareness of those around them. Our staff will only intervene in matters of safety or when behavior is deemed unruly, combative, or disruptive to the overall performance.

title: Lit Lovers Book Group
description:
Book Club, Adults

Lit Lovers is an eclectic reading group with a primary focus on fiction, while also exploring memoirs, short stories, biographies and autobiographies, mysteries, science fiction, and select works of nonfiction. The group is known for its lively, thoughtful discussions and makes a concerted effort to respect differing viewpoints. To keep conversations focused and meaningful, social chatter, gossip, and romance novels are generally kept outside the allotted discussion time.Lit Lovers gravitate toward modern fiction distinguished by strong writing, well-developed characters, and compelling narratives. Common themes include contemporary issues, family conflict, and the triumph of the human spirit, with a healthy appreciation for humor. Members read for both personal enrichment and enjoyment, and the group frequently selects works by international authors, books set abroad, or stories that explore multicultural perspectives.For a list of this year's book selections, click on the photo to the left or pick up a bookmark at the library!

title: Decoding the Deck: Intro to Tarot History and Symbolism
location: Manheim Township, MTP Morgan Center B
description:
Presentation, Adults, Seniors

Have you ever been curious about the history behind Tarot cards? Or maybe you bought a deck because the artwork was gorgeous, but now it’s just sitting on your shelf collecting dust? ✨Join us for an engaging, beginner-friendly workshop led by local instructor Theresa from @claritymindretreat! Perfect for history buffs and beginners alike, this session dives into the rich cultural origins and evolution of the cards-- from their roots as a 15th-century Italian parlor game to the modern day.What we'll cover:🌍 The Four Elements: How the suits connect to Earth, Air, Fire, and Water.🔢 Numerology Basics: Decoding the hidden meanings behind the numbers.👁️‍🗨️ Visual Language: How to read the symbols and storytelling hidden in the artwork.Whether you want to understand your own deck better or just love a good art history deep-dive, this class is for you!✍️⚠️ Please note: This presentation is strictly educational and focused entirely on history, art, and symbolism. No live readings will be conducted!

Multiple Grammy® nominee Martina McBride has sold over 23 million albums to date, which includes 20 Top 10 singles and six #1 hits.

In 2021 Martina unveiled her first exhibit in the Country Music Hall of Fame and Museum, titled “The Power of Her Voice”. 
Martina has released two cookbooks – the first, Around the Table, a full-color illustrated collection of her favorite recipes, hosting tips, practical menu planning advice, and themed décor inspiration. She released her second book, Martina’s Kitchen Mix: My Recipe Playlist for Real Life, in October 2018. Most recently Martina launched her own wine label, Luna & Finn, named after her beloved pets.

Kenny G’s influence transcends jazz. He has embraced pop culture and his place in it, with humor, making surprise appearances across film, television, and major brand campaigns, collaborating with contemporary artists across genres, and maintaining a vibrant online presence that continues to resonate with new generations of fans. title: The Knotwork Band Concert
description:
Music, Everyone

The Knotwork Band is a trio of musicians performing Celtic folk music, both traditional and modern. The band takes its name from Celtic knotwork, an art form particular to the ancient peoples of Ireland and Scotland where cords or lines are woven into intricate patterns and highly stylized designs. Like Celtic knotwork, the talents of the individual members are interwoven to form each piece of music.The audience can expect to hear Celtic folk music from Ireland, Scotland, England, and Brittany, as well as American and World music with ties to Celtic folk music, either musically or historically. Their wide spectrum of musical styles ranges from beautiful waltzes to exciting jigs and reels. The band’s music ranges from slow and hauntingly beautiful melodies to faster-paced and energetic pieces which will get the toes tapping. Our September concert will be a memorial concert in honor of William H. Sweger. Bill was a member of the Lititz Public Library’s Board of Trustees for 12 years and during that time held the offices of Secretary, Vice President and President. He joined the Board during the exciting years that led to the construction of the current library facility. Please join us for this memorial concert in his honor.

description:

Whether you're into sweet contemporary rom-coms, high-heat historical reads, or paranormal romance, there's a seat for you at our table! description:

Renowned as one of the greatest violinists of all time, Itzhak Perlman brings extraordinary artistry, warmth, and joy to audiences around the world. A true icon of classical music, Perlman has performed with every major orchestra and in the world’s most celebrated concert halls, earning 16 GRAMMY® Awards, multiple Emmy Awards, a Kennedy Center Honor, and the Presidential Medal of Freedom. 
In addition to his celebrated orchestral appearances, Perlman continues to captivate audiences through special programs and intimate recitals alongside longtime collaborator Rohan De Silva. A passionate advocate for music education, he and his wife Toby founded the Perlman Music Program, helping to mentor and inspire the next generation of musicians. 
Whether performing beloved classics or exploring new works, Perlman’s unmatched musicianship and enduring passion make every performance an unforgettable experience. 
Acclaimed pianist Rohan De Silva is widely recognized as one of the leading collaborative artists of his generation. Known for his sensitivity, precision, and expressive depth, De Silva has performed on the world’s most prestigious stages alongside many of today’s greatest instrumentalists. 
A longtime collaborator of Itzhak Perlman, De Silva brings a refined musical partnership that enhances every performance with nuance and balance. His artistry has been praised for its elegance and versatility, seamlessly supporting and elevating the soloist while shining in his own right. 
Together, De Silva and Perlman create an extraordinary concert experience, blending technical mastery with heartfelt musical connection.

Country music trailblazers Diamond Rio have been delivering chart-topping hits and signature harmonies for decades. Formed in the late 1980s, the band made history with their debut single “Meet in the Middle,” becoming the first country group ever to reach No. 1 with a debut release. They quickly followed with a string of hits, including “How Your Love Makes Me Feel,” “One More Day,” “Beautiful Mess,” “Unbelievable,” and “I Believe,” earning a reputation for their rich vocals and exceptional musicianship. 
With more than 6.8 million albums sold, over a billion global streams, and an impressive run of 20 Top 10 singles, Diamond Rio has remained a constant force in country music. Known for playing every note on their recordings, the band’s artistry extends beyond radio hits to acclaimed instrumental performances and genre-spanning projects, including their Grammy Award-winning Christian album, The Reason. 
A member of the Grand Ole Opry and recipient of multiple CMA, ACM, and Grammy honors, Diamond Rio continues to captivate audiences with their timeless sound and energetic live performances. Don’t miss your chance to experience one of country music’s most celebrated groups live in concert.

Dr. Robert Frick, historian and presenter, will share the stories and facts related to six events that significantly impacted the United States. The stories of the Great Chicago Fire of 1871, the Johnstown Flood of 1889, the San Francisco Earthquake of 1906, Hurricane Agnes in the Susquehanna Basin in 1972, the Asian Flu Pandemic of 1957-58, and the Sinking of the USS Indianapolis will be shared during this program. Participants should prepare for lively presentations filled with interesting facts and peppered with humor. Dr. Frick’s goal is education with a smile.

title: The Statler Experience
location: American Music Theatre, 2425 Lincoln Hwy East, Lancaster, PA, 17605, United States
description:
Tickets: $24 $34 $44
AMT Member Pre-Sale: Wednesday, March 4 at 10:00 a.m.
Public On-Sale: Friday, March 6 at 10:00 a.m. 








The Statler Experience brings the timeless harmonies of The Statler Brothers back to the stage in a heartfelt celebration featuring the next generation of Statler family talent: Wilson Fairchild (Wil & Langdon Reid) and Jack and Davis Reid. 
As sons and grandsons of original Statler Brothers members, these artists carry not only the sound — but the spirit — of one of country music’s most beloved vocal groups. Audiences will hear classic hits like “Flowers on the Wall,” “Bed of Rose’s,” “Do You Remember These,” and “Elizabeth,” delivered with the rich harmonies, warmth, and authenticity that defined the original quartet. 
Beyond the music, The Statler Experience offers personal stories, humor, and behind-the-scenes memories that connect generations of fans to the heart of the Statler legacy. It’s more than a tribute — it’s a family tradition brought to life on stage. 
If you cherish classic country, tight harmonies, and songs that stand the test of time, this is an evening you won’t want to miss.

location: Manheim Township, MTP Morgan Center B
description:

Are you brave enough to explore the haunted corners of Lancaster County? Join Uncharted Lancaster founder and local historian Adam Zurn for an evening of eerie legends, mysterious happenings, and true tales of the unexplained. This event promises a thrilling blend of history and the supernatural that will leave you glancing over your shoulder on the walk back to your car. From battlefields to backroads, Lancaster County’s long history hides more than a few restless spirits. In the Ghosts, Monsters, and Tales of Adventure presentation, Adam shares some of his favorite stories from his recent book of the same name. The presentation combines historical research, eyewitness accounts, and local folklore to reveal how the past still echoes through the present.Prepare to meet long-dead soldiers, vengeful spirits, and mysterious creatures that haunt the river valleys and hollow hills of the Susquehanna region. Some stories may chill your bones, while others will spark your sense of wonder at just how deep Lancaster’s legends run.

Dr. Robert Frick, historian and presenter, will share the stories and facts related to six events that significantly impacted the United States. The stories of the Great Chicago Fire of 1871, the Johnstown Flood of 1889, the San Francisco Earthquake of 1906, Hurricane Agnes in the Susquehanna Basin in 1972, the Asian Flu Pandemic of 1957-58, and the Sinking of the USS Indianapolis will be shared during this program. Participants should prepare for lively presentations filled with interesting facts and peppered with humor. Dr. Frick’s goal is education with a smile.

#### ***A Place to Make Art Together***

**When:** Every Other Saturday from 10am - 12pm
**Where:** [The Candy Factory](https://share.google/nqC7VtCS6IcDeBRyg)
**Cost:** Free & Open to the Public
**Ages:** All Ages

July 11, July 25, Aug 8, Aug 22, Sept 5, Sept 19, Oct 3, Oct 17, Oct 31, Nov 14, Nov 28, Dec 9, Dec 23

*Do you have creative aspirations but never seem to make the time? Do you want the companionship of others to overcome your creative blocks and “just do it”?*

title: Medicare Open Enrollment
location: Quarryville, QVL Story Corner/Early Literacy Lab
description:
Health & Wellness, Seniors

Medicare Annual Open Enrollment Appointments at Quarryville LibraryLancaster County Office of Aging runs a program called PA Medi, formerly APPRISE. This group assists those with questions about Medicare, Medicaid, and other health insurance all year round.   They will be scheduling appointments in their office: 150 N. Queen St., Lancaster, and at other sites all over the county during October – December, 2026.  Please call 717-299-7979 to set up an appointment at Quarryville Library or elsewhere. They will meet with you individually, confidentially, to go over what Medicare Plan you currently have, and to see if upcoming 2027 plans are the same, have higher premiums, are still available, etc.  If your coverage remains the same and you like it, you don’t have to do anything.  Drug or RX plans are those you can switch at this time of year. You can also switch from an Advantage Plan to another Advantage Plan or to an Original Medicare Plan. Insurance changes made during the Open Enrollment time become effective January 1, 2027.

location: Quarryville, QVL C.X. Carlson Cultural Room
description:

Registration is preferred; walk-ins will be accommodated as space allows. Best for adults and older interested teens.We welcome local immigration attorney Paige Britton, who will share her professional experience working within the U.S. immigration system over several sessions, exploring a different element each month.Naturalization – How does someone become a citizen?Learn about the pathways and possibilities for noncitizens to become U.S. citizens under American immigration law. Who may naturalize, and can you pass the civics test??This event is offered solely as information about the American legal system and should not be construed as legal advice. If you need legal counsel on this or other immigration matters, please consult a qualified immigration attorney.

Drop-in program. No registration required.Join us for a fun and engaging play session designed for children ages 2-7! Using colorful Lego Duplo blocks, kids can explore their creativity, improve fine motor skills, and build their imagination through hands-on play. This program encourages collaborative play and parent-child interaction.Perfect for young builders of all skill levels, this free program offers a relaxed and welcoming environment for families to connect and create together. description:

title: Trick-or-Treat @ the Library!
location: Ephrata, EPH 1/2 Multipurpose Room Kitchen Side
description:

Come in your costume and with your candy caddy! We will be walking around the Library wishing a Happy Holiday to the librarians and not only getting candy from them but also GIVING out candy to the patrons we meet. Families can bring along one bag of individually wrapped candies for the children to disperse IF that is financially possible. We will be talking about the importance of fairness and figuring out whether people want to be scared or not. Ages 0-5.

title: DNA & Dead Ends: Cracking Family Mysteries
description:
Presentation, Adults, Seniors

DNA doesn't lie!Eric Schubert will share real-life past examples from his work as a professional genealogist and forensic genetic genealogist which includes long-lost family discoveries and historic cold case breakthroughs. Attendees will learn practical strategies for starting or advancing their own research, from record paper trails to working with DNA matches. This program will offer a narrative of Eric’s research journey, as well as clear, accessible guidance for beginners and those with specific genealogical questions. These tips are inspired by experience solving complex cases for thousands across the country!Ages 18+Space is limited · Registration is required

title: Swoon Squad: A Romance TBR Book Club
location: Manheim Township, MTP Morgan Center A
description:
Book Club, Adults, Seniors

Swoon Squad is a romance-centered book club with a twist. Instead of everyone reading the same assigned title, we choose a monthly trope and invite you to pick any book that fits the theme! Whether you're into sweet contemporary rom-coms, high-heat historical reads, or paranormal romance, there's a seat for you at our table! How it Works: Pick Your Own Adventure: We announce the month's trope, and you choose a book from your own TBR pile or the library shelves that features it. Low Pressure, High Fun: No more scrambling to finish a specific book you might not even like. Read at your own pace and bring your honest thoughts! The Discussion: We gather to swap recommendations, vent about our favorite (and least favorite) clichés, and discover new authors through each other's picks.Come ready to share your pick, discuss the tropes, and meet fellow romance fans in a comfortable library setting ❤️June 29 - ⚔️Enemies to Lovers ⚔️July 27 - 🥰😠Grumpy/Sunshine😠🥰August 31 - 🏆Sports Romance🏆September 28 - 📖Academic Romance📖October 26 - 🧛Paranormal Romance🧛November 30 - 🛏️Forced Proximity🛏️December 28 - 🎁Holiday Romance🎁

title: Creative Release Open Studio Saturday
description:
The Creative House of Lancaster
#### ***A Place to Make Art Together***

**When:** Every Other Saturday from 10am - 12pm
**Where:** [The Candy Factory](https://share.google/nqC7VtCS6IcDeBRyg)
**Cost:** Free & Open to the Public
**Ages:** All Ages

**Upcoming Dates**
July 11, July 25, Aug 8, Aug 22, Sept 5, Sept 19, Oct 3, Oct 17, Oct 31, Nov 14, Nov 28, Dec 9, Dec 23

*Do you have creative aspirations but never seem to make the time? Do you want the companionship of others to overcome your creative blocks and “just do it”?*

Creative Release provides spaces and resources that make artmaking accessible. Whether you’re an experienced artist or just looking to explore your creative side, Creative Release is a safe place to explore your ideas with others. Bring your ongoing projects or use the art materials available.

Don't have a project at the moment? That's just fine. I’ll have materials to share.
**What to Expect:**

* A welcoming, inclusive environment
* A variety of art materials to experiment with
* Demonstrations on how to use different art materials
* The opportunity to work on your personal projects
* The chance to meet and collaborate with fellow creatives
* A moment to relax, create, and escape the usual routine

**Who Should Join?**
Anyone and everyone! Bring an idea for a card, a knitting pattern you’ve been wanting to try, a shirt that needs mending, or a full-on canvas and paints. Most of all, bring your lovely self! We believe in the power of community and creativity.

[Event Link](https://www.jodavis.art/community-events-1/creative-release)

Tickets: Tickets for the Night Shift are just $65 and include activity guides, a hands-on STEM workshop, snacks, and breakfast. This program is limited to children ages 6-12 and one adult (18+) is required for every three children. No adults will be admitted without children.

title: Creative Release Open Studio Saturday
description:
The Creative House of Lancaster
#### ***A Place to Make Art Together***

**When:** Every Other Saturday from 10am - 12pm
**Where:** [The Candy Factory](https://share.google/nqC7VtCS6IcDeBRyg)
**Cost:** Free & Open to the Public
**Ages:** All Ages

**Upcoming Dates**
July 11, July 25, Aug 8, Aug 22, Sept 5, Sept 19, Oct 3, Oct 17, Oct 31, Nov 14, Nov 28, Dec 9, Dec 23

*Do you have creative aspirations but never seem to make the time? Do you want the companionship of others to overcome your creative blocks and “just do it”?*

Creative Release provides spaces and resources that make artmaking accessible. Whether you’re an experienced artist or just looking to explore your creative side, Creative Release is a safe place to explore your ideas with others. Bring your ongoing projects or use the art materials available.

Don't have a project at the moment? That's just fine. I’ll have materials to share.
**What to Expect:**

* A welcoming, inclusive environment
* A variety of art materials to experiment with
* Demonstrations on how to use different art materials
* The opportunity to work on your personal projects
* The chance to meet and collaborate with fellow creatives
* A moment to relax, create, and escape the usual routine

**Who Should Join?**
Anyone and everyone! Bring an idea for a card, a knitting pattern you’ve been wanting to try, a shirt that needs mending, or a full-on canvas and paints. Most of all, bring your lovely self! We believe in the power of community and creativity.

[Event Link](https://www.jodavis.art/community-events-1/creative-release)

description:
Every First Friday the Lancaster Science Factory offers free admission from 5 – 7pm for the first 300 guests. Explore over 80 interactive exhibits for kids in grades K – 8 and their families! This program is possible through the generous support of PPL. 
  
CHILDREN MUST BE ACCOMPANIED BY AN ADULT

title: Night Shift at Lancaster Science Factory
location: The Lancaster Science Factory, 454 New Holland Ave, Lancaster, PA, 17602, United States
description:
Night Shift 2026-27  
Overview: Experience the Lancaster Science Factory in a whole new way when you stay overnight! Explore over 75 hands-on exhibits, enjoy a pre-lights-out snack, unroll your sleeping bag in the exhibit hall, and have a light breakfast before you leave in the morning. New to this year, educators will be leading hands-on STEM workshops in our Maker Space! Consider joining us for the Night Shift with your scout group, sports team or even for a special birthday!  
Tickets: Tickets for the Night Shift are just $65 and include activity guides, a hands-on STEM workshop, snacks, and breakfast. This program is limited to children ages 6-12 and one adult (18+) is required for every three children. No adults will be admitted without children.   
Dates:  
Saturday, November 7-Sunday, November 8, 2026  

Click here to register 

Saturday, December 5-Sunday, December 6, 2026  

Click here to register 

Saturday, February 13-Sunday, February 14, 2027

Itinerary:

title: Night Shift at Lancaster Science Factory
location: The Lancaster Science Factory, 454 New Holland Ave, Lancaster, PA, 17602, United States
description:
Night Shift 2026-27  
Overview: Experience the Lancaster Science Factory in a whole new way when you stay overnight! Explore over 75 hands-on exhibits, enjoy a pre-lights-out snack, unroll your sleeping bag in the exhibit hall, and have a light breakfast before you leave in the morning. New to this year, educators will be leading hands-on STEM workshops in our Maker Space! Consider joining us for the Night Shift with your scout group, sports team or even for a special birthday!  
Tickets: Tickets for the Night Shift are just $65 and include activity guides, a hands-on STEM workshop, snacks, and breakfast. This program is limited to children ages 6-12 and one adult (18+) is required for every three children. No adults will be admitted without children.   
Dates:  
Saturday, November 7-Sunday, November 8, 2026  

Click here to register 

Saturday, December 5-Sunday, December 6, 2026  

Click here to register 

Saturday, February 13-Sunday, February 14, 2027  

Click here to register 

Saturday, April 17-Sunday, April 18, 2027  

Click here to register 

Itinerary:  

6:30-7:00 pm: Arrival, check in 


7:00-10:00 pm: Museum exploration, Science Cafe activity, scavenger hunts, workshops 


7:15-7:55: Group A workshop 


8:05-8:45: Group B workshop 


8:55-9:25: Group C workshop 


10:00-10:30 pm: Set up sleeping accommodations 


10:30 pm: Get ready for lights out 


7:00-8:00 am: Light breakfast available 


8:30 am: Exhibit hall closes 

Questions? Reach out to mstoltzfus@tlsf.org
